sections.html:
• Scientific name: Metaloricaria nijsseni (Boeseman, 1976)
  • Type locality: Sipaliwini River, southwestern Suriname.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2021).
Family: Loricariidae. Common name: none. Synonym: Harttia nijsseni. Size: 29.5 cm. Temperature: 25–30°C. pH: 6.0–7.0.
South America: Suriname, Saramacca, Nickerie and Corantijn River basins. Guyana waters, coastal rivers of the Guianas, Suriname coastal rivers.

South America: Suriname, Saramacca, Nickerie, and Corantijn River basins. Type locality: Sipaliwini River, southwestern Surinam.

The species is widespread in the Corantijne, Sipaliwini, Nickerie, Saramacca, and Suriname drainages. It has a wide distribution with an extent of occurrence (EOO) of 77,184 km2 and an area of occupancy (AOO) of 13,568 km2. Therefore, this species is assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2023).

Not kept very often, but its requirements would be similar to those of the Harttia genus: they are not the easiest species to keep, as they need clean, oxygen-rich water, a large tank and a strong current.
Dry foods, algae wafers, Spirulina and normal tablet foods. Frozen foods, Artemia nauplii, glass worms and Daphnia.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Similar to the Rineloricaria and Pseudoloricaria genera. The genus Metaloricaria has a very wide lower lip. There are only two species in this genus, the other being M. paucidens from the Morani and Oyapock rivers in French Guiana.

Etymology: the specific name nijsseni is named in honour of Dr. Han Nijssen.
